label: Convexity
notes: This lecture covers printed pages 168 through 174 and states the Atiyah-Guillemin-Sternberg convexity theorem. For an effective Hamiltonian torus action on a compact connected symplectic manifold, the moment map has connected fibers and a convex polytope image. Set the stage as the climax of moment-map theory before toric geometry.

label: Setup and Hypotheses
notes: Emphasize that every hypothesis earns its keep. Compactness and connectedness keep the image bounded and convex, the torus makes components of the moment map commute, and effectiveness pins the polytope dimension. Stress that the codomain is the dual of the torus Lie algebra, here identified with real Euclidean space.

label: The AGS Theorem
notes: Read the two conclusions slowly. Connected fibers is the analytic heart; the convex polytope image is the visible payoff. The punchline is that the polytope equals the convex hull of the finite set of fixed-point images, so a finite amount of data determines the entire moment picture for the action.

label: Local Normal Form
notes: Near a fixed point the action linearizes into rotations in symplectic planes with integer weights. The moment map becomes an affine projection in those squared radial coordinates, so locally the image is a corner of a cone. This local model is what makes the global components behave like Morse functions.

label: Morse-Bott Components
notes: Pick a generic direction and pair it with the moment map to get a real function. Its critical set is the fixed-point set, and the local normal form forces every index and coindex to be even. Even indices mean level sets never disconnect, which is the connectedness engine driving the whole proof.

label: Connectedness of Fibers
notes: Walk through the induction. Connectedness for subtori of dimension one comes from Morse theory with even indices. An integer matrix selects a codimension-one subtorus, and connectedness of its projected fibers feeds the next dimension. The induction climbs from circles up to the full torus.

label: Convexity from Slicing
notes: Here connectedness becomes geometry. A connected projected fiber maps under the moment map onto a line segment, because a connected subset of a line containing two endpoints contains everything between. Sliding the slicing direction sweeps these segments across the image, proving the whole image is convex.

label: Image is the Fixed-Point Hull
notes: Explain the converse containment. A separating functional in a rationally independent direction attains its maximum on a fixed-point component, so no point outside the convex hull of fixed-point images can lie in the image. Together with convexity this pins the polytope exactly as that hull.

label: Example: Sphere and CP^1
notes: The height function on the two-sphere is the moment map for the rotation circle, with image the interval between the south and north pole values. The same picture is the standard circle action on complex projective line. One interval, two fixed points at its endpoints, the simplest convexity instance.

label: Polytope Gallery
notes: Show the family. Complex projective n-space gives a simplex with n plus one vertices, so projective plane gives a triangle. A product of two projective lines gives a square with four fixed points at its corners. Each vertex is a fixed point, and edges carry circle stabilizers, foreshadowing toric manifolds.

label: Effectiveness and Recap
notes: Close with what effectiveness buys: a nondegenerate polytope with at least m plus one vertices and the dimension bound dim M at least 2m. Recap the logic chain from even Morse indices to connected fibers to convex hull of fixed points, and point ahead to Delzant polytopes and symplectic toric manifolds.
